comment: The Linux half of the vendoring rule. On macOS 'vendored or statically linked'
has an unambiguous reading, because the app bundle carries everything. A deb
cannot: it links the platform's C library, its C++ runtime and the GTK/WebKit
stack the distribution owns. So the rule becomes an explicit, reviewed list —
these sonames, from these distribution packages, for these reasons — and the
installed-artifact audit rejects everything else. A library appearing in a
build is not an argument for adding it here; the entry is the decision.

baseline.reason: The floor the packages are certified against. Artifacts requiring a versioned symbol above these would install on 24.04 and fail to start, which is the failure mode the audit exists to prevent.

allowedRuntimeLibraries.reason: The platform C library. Not vendorable: the kernel ABI, NSS and the dynamic loader are the distribution's.

The unwinder Rust's panic machinery uses. Ships with the toolchain the distribution's compiler installed; statically linking it across a process that also loads the distribution's C++ stack would give two unwinders.
GTK/WebKit are built against it, so the process loads it whether or not Kanna's own code does.
The webview. Bundling a browser engine is not on the table, and a Kanna-shipped copy would never get the distribution's security updates.

The toolkit Tauri's Linux backend is written against, plus the rendering and accessibility libraries it exposes in its own API. Shipping a second GTK beside the session's would break theming, input methods and accessibility.
GTK's and WebKit's object system and main loop. Loaded by them, so a bundled copy would be a second incompatible instance in one process.
WebKitGTK's HTTP stack, loaded by WebKit itself.

Only permitted where a `native-tls` consumer has not yet been vendored through `openssl-src`. Every Kanna-owned TLS consumer should link the vendored copy; the audit records which artifacts still need this so the exception stays visible rather than becoming the norm.

Pulled in through GTK/WebKit's image and compression paths, and loaded by them; a bundled second zlib in the same process is a known source of subtle corruption. Measured on the desktop binary, 2026-09-09.

MEASURED EXCEPTION. First recorded 2026-09-09 on the Phase 2 dev VM (aarch64 Ubuntu 26.04) against four artifacts; confirmed 2026-09-10 on the actual supported floor by CI run 34439249468 on Ubuntu 24.04 (noble), both amd64 and arm64: kanna-worker, kanna-daemon, kanna-server, kanna-task-transfer and kanna-terminal-recovery link this dynamically, because libghostty-vt-sys's build script emits `cargo:rustc-link-lib=c++`. The preferred answer is a static link. Only libc++.a and libc++abi.a have been observed in the pinned Zig toolchain's own cache; a static libunwind archive and a working static trio (correct linker ordering against Rust's own libgcc_s unwinder) remain unverified, so this entry is a bridge, not a decision. Every build reports which artifacts still use it. Named follow-up: once a coherent static trio is verified, patch the build script to `static=c++`/`static=c++abi`/`static=unwind` against the Zig-built archives, then move these sonames back to vendoredNotDeclared. On the SUPPORTED floor, `libc++1` resolves to `libc++1-18` from `llvm-toolchain-18` in noble universe, confirmed available on both amd64 and arm64.

First recorded 2026-09-09 on the Phase 2 dev VM (aarch64 Ubuntu 26.04) against four artifacts; confirmed 2026-09-10 on the actual supported floor by CI run 34439249468 on Ubuntu 24.04 (noble), both amd64 and arm64: kanna-worker, kanna-daemon, kanna-server, kanna-task-transfer and kanna-terminal-recovery link this dynamically, because libghostty-vt-sys's build script emits `cargo:rustc-link-lib=c++`. The preferred answer is a static link. Only libc++.a and libc++abi.a have been observed in the pinned Zig toolchain's own cache; a static libunwind archive and a working static trio (correct linker ordering against Rust's own libgcc_s unwinder) remain unverified, so this entry is a bridge, not a decision. Every build reports which artifacts still use it. Named follow-up: once a coherent static trio is verified, patch the build script to `static=c++`/`static=c++abi`/`static=unwind` against the Zig-built archives, then move these sonames back to vendoredNotDeclared. On the SUPPORTED floor, `libc++abi1` resolves to `libc++abi1-18` from `llvm-toolchain-18` in noble universe, confirmed available on both amd64 and arm64. That same package's own `Depends` (`libunwind-18 >= 1:18.1.3`) is what introduces `libunwind.so.1`, declared below.

MEASURED EXCEPTION, 2026-09-10, CI run 34439249468 on Ubuntu 24.04 (noble), both amd64 and arm64: kanna-worker, kanna-daemon, kanna-server, kanna-task-transfer and kanna-terminal-recovery link this dynamically. It is transitive in provenance -- Noble's `libc++abi1-18` package (the source of the already-accepted libc++abi exception above, from the same `llvm-toolchain-18` source) depends on `libunwind-18 (>= 1:18.1.3)`; Kanna's own build script never asks for it directly -- but direct in the shipped ELF closure, so it must be declared and audited here rather than relied on silently through apt's transitive resolution. `libunwind-18` is noble universe, built from the same `llvm-toolchain-18` source as the already-accepted libc++/libc++abi exception, Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions. `libunwind-18-dev` is build-time only and must never appear as a runtime Depends. Same named follow-up as libc++/libc++abi above: move to vendoredNotDeclared once a coherent static trio is verified against the Zig-built archives.

vendoredNotDeclared.reason: SQLite is bundled through rusqlite and must stay bundled: the server owns the schema and its migrations, so a distribution-supplied SQLite would put the database's engine outside Kanna's control.

userManagedPrerequisites.comment: Not Kanna's to install and deliberately not package dependencies. Exactly the macOS boundary: launching Kanna needs none of them; running an agent task needs whichever the task's repository and provider need.
